title: Limit Laws for Incremental Propensity Score Effects with Diverging Odds Multipliers
banked_reason: Cold-tier verdict: tier=subfield; paper_score_ceiling=7.1 < 7.4; meets_floor=false; salvageable=false; no bounded field-lifting correction was overlooked.
gap_reasons: the delivered results give separated asymptotic branches and branchwise inference but no single data-driven procedure through either transition
feasible nuisance replacement/calibration is restricted to the one-dimensional smooth-boundary Bernoulli subclass while the broader marked regular-variation class is oracle-only
the ambient efficiency result is not class-intrinsic/minimax
the package lacks an implemented application or numerical calibration study
proof_attempt_summary: The run derived and internally validated a three-regime hardening theory, including the marked critical law, residual-stable endpoint, separated-regime feasible calibration, fixed-multiplier reduction, and ambient Gaussian efficiency argument; the math referee passed and all eight source checks were independently attested. It missed field tier because feasible inference remains confined to a one-dimensional C² Bernoulli subclass and does not adapt through either transition. Reaching field tier would require a new transition-adaptive procedure, broader feasible marked-tail theory, or a class-intrinsic minimax efficiency result rather than a bounded repair of this note.
tldr: Binary incremental propensity interventions avoid a fixed positivity condition only while their odds multiplier remains moderate. On a second-order regularly varying lower-propensity class, the cross-fitted incremental-mean score instead has a hardening frontier indexed by \(h_n=\delta_n/a_n\): a Gaussian law below the frontier, a compensated marked infinitely-divisible law at it, and a residual stable law above it. The critical jump retains both the treated outcome residual and the propensity-path treatment contrast. The project derives these laws, proves oracle replacement and relative consistency of an explicit cross-fitted score-variance estimator on a nonparametric \(C^2\) class, estimates the tail normalizer and joint boundary marks, certifies numerical Lévy inversion, and establishes branchwise uniform coverage. The Gaussian branch carries an oracle ambient pointwise convolution bound over \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{RV}}\), with feasible attainment asserted only on \(\mathcal P_{C^2}\).
gap: Published IPSI inference holds over fixed compact multiplier sets, while published weak-overlap stable and infinitely-divisible results concern fixed inverse-weight targets or externally trimmed scores. Neither literature handles a moving binary incremental target whose score itself changes at the rare-treatment scale.
fill: The paper constructs the three-regime law, a concrete cross-fitted boundary learner, an explicit empirical variance of held-out fitted scores, empirical tail and joint-mark estimates, and confidence intervals whose uniform coverage includes nuisance and variance replacement, logarithmic normalizer sensitivity, anti-concentration, and deterministic inversion error.
